extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and newsroom staff (and journalists seeking Reuters editorial guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and ethical guidance for Reuters journalists on how to gather and report news, emphasizing core values (independence, integrity, accuracy) and professional responsibilities. Intended to guide decision‑making rather than enumerate rigid rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Everything we do as Reuters journalists has to be independent"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is a core value derived from the Reuters Trust Principles and should inform all reporting and editorial decisions; journalists must avoid influences that compromise autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism must be free from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should strive for impartiality in selection, presentation and interpretation of facts; being free from bias is part of living the Reuters Trust Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold integrity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must act honestly and ethically in newsgathering and publication; integrity is governed in part by the Reuters Code of Conduct and is non‑negotiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters values accuracy as central to its reputation as a reliable news service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be factually correct; accuracy underpins trust and should not be sacrificed even in competitive, real‑time contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Speed is a valued attribute for a real‑time, competitive news service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While timeliness is important, speed must not override accuracy or integrity; balance rapid reporting with verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusivity is one of the valued attributes (alongside accuracy and speed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue exclusive stories responsibly, ensuring standards of verification and ethics are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Reuters Trust Principles and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavior is governed by the Reuters Trust Principles and the Reuters Code of Conduct, with a few journalist‑specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should read and apply these documents as the primary governance for conduct, decision‑making and conflict resolution; the Code complements the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for and report the truth fairly and honestly
rubrics_metrics.description: "To search for and report the truth, fairly, honestly and unfailingly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be motivated by an earnest effort to uncover and present truth, with fairness, honesty and consistency as guiding behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is identified as a 'cardinal sin'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never present others' work as your own; attribute sources properly and avoid copying text or ideas without acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabrication is described as dishonest and a cardinal sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent facts, quotes, sources or events; ensure all reported information is verifiable and grounded in evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bribe‑taking and corrupt practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Bribe‑taking is described as immoral and unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject payments or benefits that could influence reporting; maintain independence from sources of improper influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor ethical guiding principles over rigid rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Handbook is not intended as a collection of rules; it maps ethical guiding principles rather than rigid rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use principles to guide decisions when specifics are not covered; principles are meant to liberate responsible journalism and enable sound judgement rather than constrain action with inflexible rules.
